P4e: a castle precinct is sited before the streets by the mesh editor's rules on the site (size by town radius with step-down, edge in 85% of towns, backed away from the approach roads, inside the wall, clear of water, roads and the civic centre) and raised after them as a castle feature (curtain, gate, approach, moat) with works from the mesh editor's style builder (buildFortressPlanOnRing, resolveCastleStyle). A detached castle outside the town and the mesh editor's relief/terrain siting are not generated; when no site fits, castle-unplaced.
seedVectorCivicCentre reserves it, sized by population (civicSizeForPopulation, P0b). Not the mesh editor's plaza or market rules.
As plaza: a chapel below 3,000 people (drawn as massing), the catalogue basilica above; adds a cemetery.

P5b: read as the skeleton's port setting. A sea harbour is generated on the coast of a town with no river, inside an open or opening waterfront of a walled town (P5b-2); a closed sea wall leaves room for it only on some coasts. River towns get river ports (P5b-3).
P6h: read from the requested settings, else the FMG burg's shanty flag; raises the extramural shanty.
Not read by meshless generation.

P5b-2: read as the skeleton's wallCoast. auto resolves as the mesh editor (a port leaves its waterfront open, any other shore is walled); open drops the wall's longest sea-side run and opening a gap of about 120 m nearest the centre, each end carried to the shore. An open line has no circuit, so no old-town wall or town moat rides on it (diagnostics). seaWall keeps the closed line 6 m off the sea, as before.
Not read by meshless generation.
P4a: stone or wood as chosen, else stone from 1,500 people (resolveWallMaterial); sets the wall thickness (4.5 / 2.4 m) and the 3D wall body.

P4d: circulade and bram are laid from the mesh editor's vector planners (planCirculadeLayout, planPolygonalCirculadeLayout) around the site centre, sized to the built-up disc, before the routed streets; auto resolves as resolveEffectiveLayout (concentric plans only on maps of 700 m or less); both keep one wall. Rings break at water, the civic precinct and walls, because meshless keeps its own civic centre instead of the planner's small plaza and temple (P6). classic fills each district (skeleton block) with the mesh editor's classic block infill (buildPerimeterBlocks classic: Voronoi neighbourhoods of rows and lanes) instead of the organic streets; the mesh editor applies it per mesh cell, meshless per district.

rows.mesh: organic | round | oval | square | polygon | bastioned
rows.evidence: P4a: the skeleton-first shape families (unitWallShape: organic, round, oval, square, polygon, bastioned outline; auto by seed, bastioned only from the age of exploration) drawn as a closed wall on the site; the site grows by the shape's area share. The outline is turned (48 steps, each checked by building its gates) until roads and rivers cross it at 20 degrees or more, where the mesh editor squares it at rivers. Approach roads that end outside or in the wall are continued to just inside it.
P4a: polygon and bastioned outlines take the side count (3-12; unset 5-8 from the seed, as the skeleton).

P4b: generated from townWallRings double: an old-town wall of the outer outline scaled about the centre to the walled share (walledAreaShare, default 45%), nested as a child circuit. Outer-first (default) cuts it into the laid streets, easing the line by up to a few tens of percent until every crossing takes a clean gate; when none does it is left out with the inner-wall-unplaced diagnostic, as the mesh editor falls back to a single wall (about 1 in 5 generated towns, mostly bastioned outlines).

P4b: inner-first walls the old town before the streets; approach roads are continued through it and the streets reach it only through those gates. When land between the walls is then unreachable (a river cutting the ring) it falls back to outer-first with the inner-first-fallback diagnostic.
P4b: razed leaves the old-town line as boulevard roads as wide as the main roads, broken where water runs through it; the streets cross it freely.
Not read.
P4b: sizes the old-town wall of a double-walled town. A single wall still encloses the whole site (the mesh editor insets it to the share).

Reserved as a civic feature sized by population (P0b); holds a market day with aisles and stalls (P6b). Coastal sites get no civic centre yet.

P6b: a market day on the civic plaza by the mesh editor's market rules (layoutMarketStalls, cut from placeMarketInArea): aisles from each street meeting the plaza to a hub, six catalogue stalls in two rows along the long sides. Not yet: harbour and street markets, market halls, the market-area operation; a plaza under about 1,000 people is too small for a stall (market-unplaced).
Chapel or basilica by population (P0b); a chapel has no catalogue model.

P6c: the mesh editor's founding rules (monasteryKindsFor: faith and period; monasteryCountFor: town size) and precinct planner (fitMonastery) on the meshless land blocks, scored as placeMonasteries; stored as fixed precincts (environment.monasteries) drawn as massing. Not yet: a walled town's abbey outside the walls (the site has no ground there: monastery-unplaced), the catalogue's precinct models, FMG cities.

P6a: sited by burial culture zoning (churchyard, extramural roadside, riverbank) and laid out by the culture; cemetery-unplaced when no ground fits. Standalone towns only (FMG cities have no civic centre yet).

P6d: the FMG economy's guilds (planGuildFacilities) placed by the mesh editor's rules (placeGuildWorks, now given a cell-free view): a chapter's hall (with a belfry for a prestigious cloth guild) in a core land block, yards beside the approach roads beyond the town (the site grows to take them), a bleaching field on a river bank upstream; stored as environment.guilds and drawn as massing. Not yet: tanneries, craftsman streets, the catalogue's hall models, standalone towns (no economy).

P6e: the FMG economy's inns and caravanserais on the approach with the most recorded traffic, by the mesh editor's rules (placeInnsOnApproach, cut from placeGateInns): largest yard first, beyond the town edge beside the road; stored as environment.inns and drawn as a ring of rooms round the stable yard. Not yet: the gate plaza and commerce facilities (approachCommerce), the commerce inn's seat and through-yard, standalone towns (no economy).
Not generated. P6f took the mesh editor's free-standing aerial landmarks (windmills, gallows) as its own row; placed asset instances stay here.

P6f: the mesh editor's rules, cut cell-free (placeWindmillsAroundTown, placeGallowsOnApproach, windmillCountFor): post mills from the high medieval period and tower mills from the late, beyond the town edge or the walls' glacis, as many as the FMG economy's wind capacity or one per ~1,400 buildings (fewer on a river), facing into the FMG prevailing wind; the gallows mound 130-520 m out beside an approach road for 400+ buildings. Stored as environment.landmarks and drawn flat (mound, tower, sails, pillars). Not yet: elevation scoring (flat site until P8), fields and buildings as obstacles, 3D mill and gallows models, the facility-count overrides.

rows.mesh: merchant / craftsmen / patriciate wards and craft streets
rows.evidence: P6g: the mesh editor's inner ward mix (fillInner via the new cell-free assignWardMix): the FMG economy's craftsman streets by guild practitioners, merchant streets by commerce rank, market, patriciate, slum, administration, military and park (or the documented 35-slot mix without an economy), each street block of the town (inside the wall, or the core of an open town) scored by rateLocation; stored on urban.districts (ward, craftDomain) and feeding the house storeys (patriciate rich, merchant and market commercial; vector-urban-v14). Not yet: gate wards, the approachCommerce market street, ward-specific lot sizes, gardens and archetypes (medievalFabric), ward tints.

P6h: the mesh editor's pickShanty (cell-free pickShantySpots): 3-6 street blocks beyond the wall in the band out to 1.8 times its reach, in the cone of the busiest approaches, nearest the wall first; ward shanty on urban.districts, built up whatever the demand. A site ending at the wall first grows by a strip along the two busiest approaches (land of its own, so blocks inside the wall never merge with it). Not yet: an open town's shanty band, ward-specific shanty fabric.

rows.mesh: harbour ward, quays, cargo, cranes, warehouses
rows.evidence: P5b: generated on sea coasts by the mesh editor's harbour planner on cell-free shores (planHarborOnShores): quays, loading yards, cranes, crane quays, cargo piles, piers, street accesses; stored as a fixed harbour plan. River shores take short bank piers (a quarter of the channel) and barges (P5b-3). Not yet: harbour presets, warehouses, the whole-bank quay strips.
P5b: generated with the harbour by the mesh editor's ship planner (planShipsAtPiers): pier berths, anchorage, crane quays and lighters; ships the stored plan cannot re-solve are left out.

P5b-3: river ports on a fixed river (its site water, or a fixed river path) by the shared harbour planner: bank quays, short piers, barges; 29 of 32 synthesized river towns. P5b-4: ferries where FMG crosses a river by ferry (the period has no bridge for it): the road ends on the town bank, and the mesh editor's figure-of-eight crossing (planFerryCrossing) is stored with jetties, landings and towpaths, whose ground is kept from houses and the harbour. Not yet: the far-bank road, ferry boats.
